architecture_principles: the unit of decision is an experiment, not a formulation
value of information is computed by a deterministic scientific tool, not by an additional language model
every registered hypothesis carries an explicit pre-result prediction rule and an explicit falsification condition
a measurement that cannot separate any registered hypothesis scores zero discrimination, and that is a scientific result rather than a defect
weight sensitivity is reported as decision stability, never as model confidence
ties in the deterministic layer are reported as ties; the tool must not manufacture a preference it does not have
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
the mechanism question and the Agent framework are separate contributions and are reported separately

candidate_space.rationale: V4 deliberately reuses the byte-identical V3 lattice. Continuous-space optimization and any new wet-lab work are out of scope, so that the measured change between V3 and V4 is the decision object and the VOI layer, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> evidence/tool layer (including the deterministic VOI tool) -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze
architecture.claim_boundary: V4.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime. Its adjudication tests whether a registered hypothesis survives contact with the completed measurement. It is not a contemporaneous pre-experimental record and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_VOI_GUIDED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V4
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
turning the study into a pure AI benchmark
weakening or replacing the rheological mechanism result
architecture.purpose: Outcome-blind scientific decision Agent that selects the next formulation x measurement EXPERIMENT by transparent value of information, rather than selecting a formulation candidate alone.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question that the next experiment must answer, then request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations

execute read-only scientific tools, including the paper-derived state-aware rheology tool, external evidence retrieval, and the deterministic VOI tool that scores every formulation x measurement experiment card
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value, stating the hypotheses it separates and what each possible outcome would establish
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability of the primary observable, and whether the stated falsification criterion can actually be met by the measurement
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported VOI weight sensitivity and the skeptic's strongest objection
commit to one experiment card, or abstain, and state the acceptance and falsification criteria that will adjudicate it
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card with timestamps, model identifiers and cryptographic hashes of every input

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V4 is an independent architecture. configs/agent_v3.json, prompts/agent_v3_*.txt, src/pur_new/agent_v3.py and every frozen V3 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V4.

voi_tool.explicitly_not: distance to any held-out formulation. No target coordinate enters any component, weight or tie-break.
voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk
voi_tool.name: score_experiment_cards
voi_tool.not_a_posterior: The local design contains six audited realizations and two thermal-hold trajectories. That does not support a calibrated Bayesian expected-information computation, so no posterior probability is fabricated. Weight sensitivity is reported instead.

decision_stability_sent_to_model.metric_is_not: model confidence; posterior probability; calibrated expected information
decision_stability_sent_to_model.tie_interpretation: The deterministic VOI layer is indifferent among the tied top experiments: they share an identical component vector. Tie-breaking is therefore a genuine task left to the Agent, and any selection inside this set cannot have been read off the VOI ranking.
decision_stability_sent_to_model.voi_formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.

evidence_policy.description: For prospective/blind Agent evaluation. The Agent may see original-system measurements and external analogue evidence, but not the target validation formulation identity, its wet-lab outcome, or any outcome-derived labels.

judge_normalized.acceptance_criterion: Run at least two independent repeats and calculate SI_15_60 for each. Accept the combined dual-axis intervention as supporting H-RESIN over H-CORE if every repeat has SI_15_60 < 3.80%, which is below half of the H-CORE linear-dilution prediction of 7.61% for reactive mass fraction 0.8000.
judge_normalized.falsification_criterion: Using the arithmetic mean of the independent-repeat SI_15_60 values, a mean SI_15_60 >= 7.61% falsifies H-RESIN's superlinear-suppression prediction and supports H-CORE at the registered resolution. Conversely, a mean SI_15_60 < 3.80% falsifies H-CORE's linear-dilution prediction; intermediate means do not decisively falsify either hypothesis. Neither outcome separates H-RESIN from H-DUAL.
judge_normalized.next_experiment_if_falsified: Run a matched acrylic-only 15.0% AC1920 composition with 0% TK100 using the same E2 reactive-core basis, 120 C M-HOLD-120 protocol, independently prepared repeats, recorded preparation history, and a common-temperature realized-viscosity anchor.
judge_normalized.primary_observable: SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15, percent, measured at 120 C over the 15-60 min matched window
judge_normalized.rationale: S1C41 combines 15% AC1920 and 5% TK100 while preserving the E2 reactive-core proportions, giving a registered H-CORE prediction of 7.61% drift and a low-drift threshold of 3.80%. M-HOLD-120 directly observes the declared 120 C viscosity-growth failure mode without model fitting or extrapolation. The selection breaks the genuine top tie toward the minimum supported intervention while retaining discrimination of the reactive-core explanation from a low-drift combined intervention.
judge_normalized.stage_disagreements_resolved: I followed the Proposer and Robustness Adjudicator in selecting S1C41 because it is in the stable deterministic top tie, directly measures the least-resolved failure coordinate, and uses the smallest supported dual-axis modifier burden. I followed the Skeptic in restricting the interpretation: the result tests only combined composition-level suppression versus linear dilution, does not separate H-RESIN from H-DUAL, cannot establish a molecular encounter-frequency mechanism, and requires explicit repeat aggregation.

uncertainty_decomposition.evidence_coverage_uncertainty: The candidate uses both modifier axes within the supported regions, but the dual-axis design cannot identify whether acrylic-like modification, minor tackifier-like modification, or their combination drives suppression.
uncertainty_decomposition.extrapolation_uncertainty: Low for the selected composition because 15% acrylic-like modifier and 5% minor tackifier-like modifier lie within the registered supported regions; external analogue evidence does not establish an exact local outcome.
uncertainty_decomposition.measurement_uncertainty: The direct matched-window observable has a declared discrimination threshold of 2.00 percentage points; at least two independent repeats are required.
uncertainty_decomposition.realization_state_uncertainty: M-HOLD-120 does not control realization state; prior 120 C matched-temperature viscosity realizations varied by up to 3.57-fold, so preparation history and repeat dispersion can confound formulation-level drift comparisons.

planner.failure_mode: Uncontrolled viscosity growth during prolonged 120 C melt residence, with its chemical origin unresolved from process-state variation.
planner.failure_mode_evidence: The original 120 C thermal holds show a large formulation contrast: E1 increased by 9.51% from 15 to 60 min, whereas E5 increased by 51.54%; separately, E2 temperature-sweep realizations varied by about 2.80-3.57-fold at matched temperatures.
planner.least_resolved_justification: The local data contain only the E1 and E5 original 120 C hold series, with four time points over 15-90 min and no matched modifier-axis comparison or follow-up hold profiles. In contrast, temperature response is sampled at six temperatures from 80-130 C across multiple E1-E3 realizations, while viscosity-level variation is explicitly observed through the E2 repeat spread.
measurement_requirements: Measure viscosity at 120 C at 15, 30, 45, and 60 min and report the matched-window SI_15_60 relative change.
Use at least two independent repeats with controlled and recorded preparation history so process-state variation can be separated from formulation effects.

Measure the realized viscosity level at a common anchor temperature before or alongside the hold, and document the temperature support, so comparisons are made at matched material state rather than nominal composition alone.

Compare the observed drift with the frozen reactive-mass linear-dilution prediction and use the same protocol for acrylic-only and tackifier-containing modifier axes when testing the dual-axis hypothesis.
planner.scientific_question: At a controlled and matched realized viscosity state, does a resin-modified composition reduce 120 C matched-window viscosity drift substantially below the reactive-core linear-dilution prediction, thereby separating the reactive-core/stoichiometry-only hypothesis from the resin-modification hypothesis; and does acrylic-only material fail to achieve that reduction relative to a composition with a non-zero minor tackifier axis?

hypotheses_not_separated: H-RESIN versus H-DUAL cannot be separated because both predict low drift for this composition; an acrylic-only hold is required for that comparison.

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: If SI_15_60 is below 3.80% across at least two repeats, the result supports H-RESIN over H-CORE and falsifies the linear-dilution prediction of 7.61% by more than the 2.00% resolution threshold. It also demonstrates low drift with both modifier axes active, but does not distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: If SI_15_60 is at or above 7.61%, H-RESIN is falsified and the reactive-core/stoichiometry-only explanation H-CORE is supported. Such a result also fails to support the low-drift prediction of H-DUAL for this dual-axis composition.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: A result between 3.80% and 7.61% indicates partial or unresolved suppression relative to linear dilution and does not decisively adjudicate H-CORE versus H-RESIN at the registered thresholds. It would warrant improved state control or a matched acrylic-only comparison before attributing the effect to either modifier axis.

proposer.primary_observable: SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15, percent, measured directly from viscosity at 120 C over 15-60 min

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: It is genuinely VOI-tied but uses 17.5% acrylic rather than the minimum supported 15%, adding modifier burden without increasing hypothesis-pair discrimination or measurement interpretability.
It is genuinely VOI-tied and has a directly commensurate 20% acrylic anchor, but the larger acrylic intervention is unnecessary for the same H-CORE versus H-RESIN/H-DUAL separation.
It is genuinely VOI-tied but moves farther toward the upper acrylic region, increasing intervention burden without adding a separable hypothesis outcome.
It is genuinely VOI-tied but uses the maximum supported acrylic loading, making it the largest justified perturbation while providing no additional registered-pair discrimination.
It retains the same direct hold discrimination but uses 7.5% tackifier, outside the repeatedly clustered 4.8-6.4% region, and therefore carries measurable extrapolation risk.

proposer.reasoning: The 120 C matched-window hold directly measures the least-resolved failure coordinate and separates two hypothesis pairs: H-CORE versus H-RESIN and H-CORE versus H-DUAL. Its observable requires no model fit or extrapolation. S1C41 is the scientifically preferred member of the real top tie because it combines both independently supported modifier axes at the smallest sufficient burden, while its outcomes remain explicitly falsifiable and its inability to distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL is clear.
proposer.tie_break_justification: S1C41 uses the smallest total modifier burden in the tied set while remaining inside both externally supported intervention regions: 15% acrylic-like modifier is the supported lower-region design point and 5% minor tackifier-like modifier lies in the repeatedly documented 4.8-6.4% cluster. It therefore preserves the same direct discrimination of H-CORE from H-RESIN and H-DUAL with less justified departure from the characterized reactive core.

residual_decision_risk: Process-state variability remains uncontrolled because M-HOLD-120 does not include the required common-temperature realized-viscosity anchor.
The proposal does not define whether thresholds apply to every repeat, the repeat mean, or another aggregation rule.
Two repeats may be insufficient given the documented 120 C realization spread of up to 3.57-fold.
The experiment cannot separate H-RESIN from H-DUAL or identify which modifier axis causes suppression.
A viscosity-hold result cannot establish the molecular encounter-frequency mechanism stated in H-RESIN.
The small base VOI margin leaves some untested weighting or scoring-model risks outside the reported perturbation sweep.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: The strongest objection is valid: the dual-axis composition simultaneously changes acrylic-like and minor-tackifier-like content, so a low SI_15_60 can reject H-CORE and demonstrate combined composition-level suppression but cannot distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL or attribute suppression to either axis. This limitation is explicitly acknowledged by the proposer and does not change the experiment for the stated performance-mitigation objective. It does require interpreting the result as evidence about the combined intervention, not as evidence for a specific modifier axis or molecular encounter-frequency mechanism. An acrylic-only matched hold would be needed as a follow-up for axis attribution.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: S1C41::M-HOLD-120 remains in the tied top set under all 25 re-weightings: top_experiment_set_stability is 1.0, measurement-plan and intervention-family stability are both 1.0, and every recommendation_flip_boundary survives the full 0.5-1.5 multiplier sweep. No tested weighting changes the decision. The 0.004583 base VOI margin to the best strictly lower experiment is small, but the absence of flips across the stated sweep is defensible because the hold directly measures the least-resolved failure coordinate, has full measurement interpretability, and uses modifier levels within the supported regions.

skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: The 120 C hold directly measures SI_15_60 at the required 15 and 60 min points, so values below 3.80% or at or above 7.61% can be produced by this protocol. The criterion is not fully robust because the proposal does not define how the two repeats are aggregated and does not control the documented process-state variability.
leakage_findings: No reliance on an unmeasured validation outcome or hidden formulation identity is evident.
The planned rheological hold cannot establish the molecular encounter-frequency mechanism stated in H-RESIN.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A low SI_15_60 result could support either general resin-modification suppression or the requirement for the minor tackifier axis; it cannot establish which modifier axis is responsible.
objections.objection: The proposer lists H-CORE, H-RESIN, and H-DUAL under "hypotheses_separated", but the dual-axis S1C41 composition (15.0% AC1920 and 5.0% TK100) cannot distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL because both predict low drift for this composition. The proposer does acknowledge this under "hypotheses_not_separated", so the claimed coverage is only partial.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Any drift below the 3.80% criterion would support only a dual-axis composition-level performance effect and H-CORE rejection; it would not support the claimed mechanism or establish that the tackifier is required.
objections.objection: The formulation changes both modifier axes simultaneously: 15.0% acrylic-like AC1920 and 5.0% minor tackifier-like TK100 replace reactive core material, giving a reactive mass fraction of 0.8000. The primary observable therefore combines dilution, acrylic effects, and tackifier effects. The planned result cannot attribute suppression to acrylic, tackifier, or their interaction, even though H-RESIN and H-DUAL make different axis-level claims.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A drift difference could be caused by realization or preparation-state displacement rather than formulation, weakening the interpretation of SI_15_60 as evidence for H-RESIN or H-DUAL.
objections.objection: SI_15_60 is directly calculated from the measured 120 C viscosities at 15 and 60 min, so it does not inherit the model-fit weakness of M-SWEEP or M-ANCHOR. However, the proposer calls the comparison "matched" while the S1C41 measurement plan contains only the M-HOLD-120 protocol and does not include the planner's required common-temperature realized-viscosity anchor or a defined rule for matching material state. The catalog also states that M-HOLD-120 does not control process state.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A threshold pass or fail could be overinterpreted as falsification of H-CORE or H-RESIN without a defined repeat-level decision rule or adequate control of realization variability.
objections.objection: The criterion "SI_15_60 is at or above 7.61%" is directly measurable, and the low-drift criterion of below 3.80% is separated from the 7.61% H-CORE prediction by more than the declared 2.00% resolution. However, "across at least two repeats" does not specify whether every repeat, the mean, or a confidence bound must cross the threshold, and M-HOLD-120 requires only two repeats despite the documented E2 matched-temperature realization spread of up to 3.57-fold. Thus the protocol can generate threshold-crossing numbers, but cannot reliably establish that the observed result is a formulation effect rather than state variation.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A low measured drift would be reported as evidence for a specific molecular explanation that the rheological protocol cannot identify.
objections.objection: The registered claim boundary correctly limits adjudication to formulation-level rheological mechanisms, but the H-RESIN statement attributes suppression to lowered effective concentration and encounter frequency of reactive species. The planned viscosity-hold measurement can establish drift behavior relative to the 7.61% linear-dilution prediction; it cannot establish that molecular or encounter-frequency mechanism. No outcome leakage is evident in the supplied proposal.

skeptic.recommended_change: Add a matched acrylic-only 15.0% AC1920 composition with TK100 at 0%, using the same reactive-core basis, M-HOLD-120 protocol, realized-viscosity anchor, and independently prepared repeats. Define the decision rule explicitly for each repeat or for the repeat mean, and record preparation history and anchor viscosity so state variation is separable from modifier-axis effects.
skeptic.strongest_objection: The composition simultaneously activates the 15.0% acrylic-like and 5.0% minor-tackifier-like axes, so the primary SI_15_60 result cannot attribute any suppression to either axis or distinguish H-RESIN from H-DUAL; it only tests a combined intervention against the linear-dilution baseline.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.

design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.

provenance_audit.reason: The source record is phosphoric-acid-labelled and its additive identity/amount is not represented in formulations.csv; it is retained as sensitivity-only until chemistry is reconciled.

minor_tackifier_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 5% represents the repeatedly documented minor-resin region and 10% is a conservative coarse upper level.

result.claim_boundary: External examples are analogues. They support candidate-family and coarse-region hypotheses, not an exact optimum for AC1920/TK100 and not a proven local molecular mechanism. The current reconstruction uses only pre-result evidence at runtime; the exact validation coordinates and outcome are excluded from candidate construction, ranking and tie-breaking.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

minor_tackifier_like.basis: Curated PUR examples repeatedly place tackifying/hydrocarbon resin near 5%, with broader guidance below about 10%.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. The current coarse grid and fine-refinement software are later reproducible operationalizations of the evidence-constrained region and are not represented as the original contemporaneous freeze algorithm unless older provenance is recovered.

local_reactive_core_anchor.reason: E2 is the geometric centre of the original five-point local design: 50/50 PPG2000/PDP-70 and NCO:OH=1.80, centered between E1/E3 stoichiometric perturbations and E4/E5 composition perturbations.
local_reactive_core_anchor.stoichiometry_note: The E2 NCO:OH=1.80 label applies to the original reactive core. If a modifier contributes reactive OH or another NCO-reactive group, true stoichiometry must be recalculated from verified material specifications.

stability_hypotheses.H1_formulation_family: Partial replacement of the reactive-only formulation by an acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like resin can reduce hot-hold viscosity drift under matched process conditions.
stability_hypotheses.H2_functionality: At comparable acrylic loading, lower effective reactive-group density or lower-OH acrylic chemistry is expected to be more favorable for hot-hold viscosity stability than more highly reactive acrylic chemistry.
stability_hypotheses.H3_region: A useful candidate region is expected within the externally supported coarse space spanned by 15-25% acrylic-like modifier and 0-10% minor tackifier-like modifier, while preserving the relative E2 reactive-core proportions.

voi_sent_to_model.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.
voi_sent_to_model.tie_note: These experiments share an identical component vector. The deterministic tool is indifferent among them. Any choice within this set must be justified scientifically.

top_cards.acceptance_criterion: Matched 15-60 min drift at 120 C stays below 3.80% across at least two repeats, i.e. below half the linear-dilution prediction of 7.61% implied by a reactive mass fraction of 0.8000. This accepts H-RESIN over H-CORE.
top_cards.falsification_criterion: H-RESIN is falsified if matched 15-60 min drift is at or above the linear-dilution prediction of 7.61%. H-CORE is falsified if drift falls below 3.80%, a separation larger than the 2.00% resolution threshold. This composition carries both axes, so it cannot separate H-RESIN from H-DUAL; an acrylic-only hold is the follow-up required for that.

measurement_plan.name: matched-window 120 C thermal hold
measurement_plan.protocol: Hold the melt at 120 C. Record viscosity at 15, 30, 45 and 60 min. Report the 15-60 min matched-window relative change. Run at least two independent repeats.
